title: preview.decide is wired to the runner in the daemon registry, and a preview can be started and offered
definitionOfDone: A well-formed preview.decide APPROVE over the real registry no longer throws PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED: it commits a durable decision readable back from /activity/read carrying its verdict. Assert the verdict from the activity read, not from the handler's return value. The current stub at daemon-command-registry.ts:438 is deleted, and `git grep -n 'preview runner is not landed'` returns 0 hits.

REJECT with findings commits a durable decision carrying those findings, each naming a nodeRef, and the named node is reworkable on the graph. Assert the persisted findings roster, not the decoded payload.

A preview can be STARTED for a landed goal by a production path, and that path writes a receipt via recordPreviewReceipt carrying {goalId, sha, url, pid, screenshots[], STARTED|REFUSED(code)}. Assert the receipt is readable from the store after the start, through the production read surface rather than the writer.

preview.decide is OFFERED on the affordance surface for a goal with a STARTED receipt, targeted at that goal, and is ABSENT when there is no receipt and when the receipt is REFUSED. Assert set-equality on commandKind@target, not a subset - a subset assertion cannot see an offer that should have disappeared.

Each of the four refusal codes is raised by the layer PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS names for it, over the REAL registry edge, with every other gate made passable so the arm pins WHICH layer answered (global rail 1). PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID @ REQUEST, PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED @ GOAL_AUTHORITY, PREVIEW_COMMAND_MISSING @ RUNNER, PREVIEW_START_TIMEOUT @ RUNNER.

Daemon shutdown sweeps live previews: createPreviewSupervisor().close() is called from the production shutdown path and a test asserts a started preview's process is gone afterwards, using preview-test-fixtures.ts:124 awaitPidGone over the production probe rather than a third liveness helper.

If a NEW runtime command kind is added (epic rail 2): the shared contract, all four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors and the regenerated client are rotated in the same commit, censused by a full-tree `git grep` of the literal across ALL file types, and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is run with its count line quoted. If no new kind is added, say so plainly instead.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines, each standalone and foreground: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Repo-wide red is attributed by the merge-base-vs-HEAD path-attributed baseline (global rail 3), disclosed verbatim, never hidden.
taskRails: COMPOSE, DO NOT REBUILD. apps/daemon/src/preview/ is landed and green (commit 6de79b6c, 93 tests). This row adds the EDGES that reach it: the registry edge, the start trigger, the affordance offer, the shutdown sweep. Re-implementing runner behaviour here is a silent duplicate that collides with its owner.

EVERY REFUSAL THROUGH `previewRefusal`. preview-contracts.ts derives the layer from the closed PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS map precisely so a call site cannot mint a code/layer pair that disagrees. Never pass a layer literal.

SHARED ROSTER CONTENTION (epic rail 3). daemon-command-registry.ts, daemon-command-families.ts and daemon-command-vocabulary.ts are contended by task-a2409cba, task-c422b106 and task-166d375f. Never freeze a count literal in a DoD or a test; run the leg and take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative.

IF A NEW KIND IS PUBLISHED (epic rail 2): census the digest mirrors with a full-tree `git grep` of the literal across ALL file types and run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`. apps/control-room is in NONE of `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` or the daemon leg, so a forgotten mirror ships two hard-throwing tests behind three green gates.

THIS ROW UNBLOCKS task-33ceae56edc348e9864bc592430fa1d0, the Gate 2 browser proof, which is BLOCKED on it. That row owns the card, the e2e journey, the live drive and the README sweep - do NOT build browser UI here.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE BEFORE PLANNING ANY EDIT (global rail 6). NO PRODUCTION EDITS IN THIS STEP — it is read-only, which is why only the registry appears in affectedFiles. Re-run the four gap legs at your claim HEAD and paste outputs in the step note: (a) `grep -n "preview runner is not landed" apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts`; (b) `git grep -n "createPreviewSupervisor\|recordPreviewReceipt\|readPreviewReceipt" -- apps packages ':!apps/daemon/src/preview/*'`; (c) `git grep -in preview -- 'apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-*.ts' | grep -v test`. Then READ and record the three shapes this plan depends on, because the plan names them but you must confirm them: (1) the exact `findings` element shape from `findingsOf` / the REJECT payload in apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-contracts.ts — specifically whether a finding carries a nodeRef and which key names it, since DoD 2 requires the persisted findings each name a nodeRef and the named node be reworkable on the graph; (2) `DurableDecision` in http/http-contract.js — which field carries a verdict back to /activity/read (apps/daemon/src/http/activity-read.ts, ACTIVITY_READ_PATH at :22) and where result bytes live, since DoD 1 and 2 assert from the ACTIVITY READ, never from the handler's return; (3) whether reaching the preview port from the daemon's async shutdown requires widening `DaemonDependencyProvider` — if it does, that file is the tenth and last slot in this row's budget, and `StoreDependencyProvider.close()` must stay SYNC (six call sites: mcp-main.ts:158, agent-wrapper-main.ts:366, four fixtures). Finally record the global-rail-3 baseline: run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck` at the MERGE-BASE and save the failing-file rosters, so HEAD red can be attributed in step 8.

WRITE THE DECIDE-EDGE ARMS FIRST, all red before any implementation (tests-first). Create apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-daemon-edge.test.ts — the filename MUST match the module created in step 3 EXACTLY, or runtime-entrypoint.test.ts classifies the module TEST tier and reports its `.js` bridge as `unexpected` (this cost task-f5a74c23 a round). Build the store with the production bootstrap; establish receipt state ONLY through `recordPreviewReceipt` (the production writer) — never by planting rows. Arms: (1) APPROVE over a STARTED receipt for a fully-landed goal commits a durable decision whose verdict is readable back from the ACTIVITY READ surface, asserted from that read, not from the handler's return value. (2) REJECT with findings commits a durable decision whose PERSISTED findings roster is read back and asserted element-by-element, each naming a nodeRef, and the named node is shown reworkable on the graph. (3) Four refusal arms, each raised over the REAL edge with EVERY OTHER GATE MADE PASSABLE so the arm pins which layer answered (global rail 1): PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID @ REQUEST (malformed payload); PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED @ GOAL_AUTHORITY (receipt absent, and separately goal not allLanded); PREVIEW_COMMAND_MISSING @ RUNNER and PREVIEW_START_TIMEOUT @ RUNNER (a REFUSED receipt carrying that code travels back UNRESTAMPED). Assert code AND layer on every one. Give each refusal group a positive control so it cannot pass vacuously. Confirm every arm is RED for the right reason before step 3.

IMPLEMENT the edge module: apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-daemon-edge.ts plus its `.js` bridge apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-daemon-edge.js (one line, `export * from "./preview-daemon-edge.ts";`, matching every sibling in that directory). It exports two things and nothing else: (a) a factory that constructs ONE `createPreviewSupervisor` and returns the port the daemon holds — its `decide`, its `close`, and a lazy receipt-state reader `(goalId) => "STARTED"|"REFUSED"|null` built on `readPreviewReceipt` for step 7's offer fact; (b) `runPreviewDecideEdge(context)`, shaped like the sibling edges in daemon-command-edges.ts and daemon-command-design.ts, returning a `DurableDecision`. Order inside the edge: decode via `decodePreviewDecidePayload`; resolve the receipt with `readPreviewReceipt` using the decoded `previewRef` as the receipt id; an absent or invalid receipt refuses PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED; a receipt already carrying a refusal code returns THAT code and layer unrestamped; confirm the goal is landed with `readGoalLandingStatus(...).allLanded`; then call the supervisor's `decide(previewRef, decision)` and commit the durable decision carrying the verdict and, for REJECT, the findings roster. EVERY refusal is minted through `previewRefusal(code)` — it takes no layer and PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS decides; passing a layer literal is a rejection (task rail 2). Keep the file under 250 physical lines. Do NOT re-implement runner behaviour (task rail 1): this module composes preview-supervisor, preview-ledger and preview-goal-landing, which are landed and green at commit 6de79b6c.

DELETE THE FAIL-CLOSED STUB and delegate. In apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts remove the whole `if (preview) { ... }` block at :434-441 — both throws, including `previewRefusal("PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED")` with the message "preview runner is not landed" — and replace it with `if (preview) return runPreviewDecideEdge(context)`, keeping its placement BEFORE `requestOf` and preserving the existing comment's reason for that placement (preview has no codec, so the assembler would refuse with the wrong code entirely). Add the preview port to `DaemonCommandPortOptions` (:107) as an OPTIONAL member, following the file's own established convention that an absent port is a REFUSING state rather than a skipped one — an unwired daemon must still fail closed with a preview code, never silently succeed or crash. Do not grow this file's responsibilities further: it is 531 lines, already past the 400-line split threshold, which is exactly why the edge lives in its own module. Verify `git grep -n "preview runner is not landed"` returns ZERO hits afterwards (DoD 1).

COMPOSE THE SUPERVISOR ONCE AND SWEEP IT ON SHUTDOWN (DoD 6). In apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts construct the preview port from step 3's factory exactly ONCE (two instances would each hold half the live roster and shutdown would sweep only one), pass it into the `createDaemonCommandPorts({...})` call at :189, and expose it on the provider so the entry can reach it. Then in apps/daemon/src/daemon-entry.ts await the port's `close()` inside the shutdown at :328-335, alongside the existing `await started.close()` — that path is ALREADY async, which is why the sweep hangs there. Do NOT widen `StoreDependencyProvider.close()` (:151, :549) to async: it is sync with six call sites (mcp-main.ts:158, agent-wrapper-main.ts:366 and four fixtures) and changing it is out of this row's scope. Add the shutdown arm to preview-daemon-edge.test.ts: start a preview through the port, drive the PRODUCTION shutdown path, and assert the child's pid is gone using `awaitPidGone` from preview-test-fixtures.ts:124, which already wraps the production probe `probeProcessAlive` — do not write a third liveness helper (DoD 6 names this explicitly).

WRITE THE OFFER ARMS FIRST, red before step 7 (DoD 4). In apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-planning-offers.test.ts add arms over the real offer resolution: preview.decide IS offered, targeted at the goal, for a goal whose receipt is STARTED; is ABSENT when there is no receipt; and is ABSENT when the receipt is REFUSED. Establish each receipt state through `recordPreviewReceipt`, the production writer. ASSERT SET-EQUALITY on the full commandKind@target roster, never a subset — DoD 4 says so for a concrete reason: a subset assertion cannot observe an offer that should have DISAPPEARED, which is exactly what the no-receipt and REFUSED cases test. Note the existing trap in this file: the `"preview.decide"` literal already at :456 is HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS membership (the fence), NOT an offer — do not read it as existing coverage and do not disturb it. Never freeze a roster COUNT literal in these arms (epic rail 3); derive the expected set, and if a count line is printed take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative.

IMPLEMENT THE OFFER. In apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-planning-offers.ts add a `previewReceipt: (goalId) => "STARTED"|"REFUSED"|null` member to `PlanningOfferInput`, following the file's own documented convention exactly: a FACT, not a store handle, and LAZY — invoked only for a goal that could actually be offered the decision, the same discipline `closeReadiness` and `landedCommit` are given at :41-62 and for the same stated reason (the ladder stays pure and the surface cost does not multiply by the goal count). Mint the offer through the local `offer(input, kind, target)` helper at :126 so it shares identity and mint-id handling with every other offer. Only a STARTED receipt is offered: a null receipt and a REFUSED receipt both withhold, fail-closed. Then in apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts supply the fact in the `resolvePlanningOffers({...})` call at :298-317, resolving it through step 3's port so the offer surface and the decide edge read the SAME receipt authority and cannot disagree. Keep the derivation per-call and uncached, matching the comments already on `landedCommit` and `closeReadiness` — a receipt written between two polls must appear on the next one.

MUTATION-DRILL EVERY FAILURE-PATH ARM, then run the gates. First the drills (global rail 1 requires each failure-path test be proven non-vacuous by mutating the PRODUCTION surface and confirming red): for each of the four refusal codes, mutate the edge to mint a different code, confirm the arm goes RED naming the expected-vs-received code AND layer, and restore. Also drill the offer arms by making the STARTED branch offer unconditionally and confirming the no-receipt and REFUSED arms go red. RESTORE PROOF (global rail 13): `git status --porcelain` every mutated path BEFORE drilling; for any path showing `??`, prove the restore by SHA256 equality against an out-of-tree backup under %TEMP% suffixed with your worker id, in a call SEPARATE from the restore — `git diff` is blind to untracked files and will show clean whether or not the bytes came back. Then run the gates, each STANDALONE and FOREGROUND, quoting the `Test Files N passed` count line for each: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. A leg that prints no count line RAN NO TESTS and is not a pass (global rail 8). In the daemon leg, read runtime-entrypoint.test.ts's `unexpected` ARRAY specifically — the expected disclosed baseline is one entry, `repository\deployment\deployment-docker-probe.js`; ANY entry containing `preview\` is this row's own bug and means the new module's test filename does not match it. Attribute repo-wide red by merge-base-vs-HEAD against step 1's saved rosters, intersect with this row's owned paths, and disclose every foreign red verbatim with its failing file paths (global rail 3).

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, then complete. Read the whole diff as an attacker: Does any refusal pass a layer literal instead of minting through `previewRefusal`? Is `createPreviewSupervisor` constructed exactly once on the production path (grep it — two instances split the live roster and shutdown sweeps only one)? What happens on a CONCURRENT decide and shutdown over the same receipt — the supervisor's `forget` removes an entry BEFORE stopping it precisely so the two stop it once between them; does the edge preserve that? Does an unwired preview port fail CLOSED with a preview code rather than crashing or silently succeeding? Does a REJECT with an empty findings roster refuse rather than commit? Can a receipt written under a different principal, kind or project be read back as this goal's — or does `readPreviewReceipt`'s re-validation still hold at the edge? Does the offer fact stay lazy, so a poll over many goals does not pay a ledger read per goal (the 09-05 affordances hot-path incident)? Then write the completion record. It MUST state plainly that THIS ROW ADDS NO NEW RUNTIME COMMAND KIND, satisfying DoD 7's second clause — `preview.start` is carried by task-0e87ab34 (shared contract) and task-dbc79d25 (daemon async command), and DoD 3 with it; see comment-0fe1031487b84ee6a0b8c2d7fb004ef0 for the clause-to-row map. Report every path you created or modified in complete_step.modifiedFiles. Four foreign dirty paths were present at claim — note them, never revert, stash or `git add -A` them.

SPIDR SPLIT + DoD SCOPE RECORD — architect-aa54e231, 2026-09-06, at PLANNING claim. Read this BEFORE grading the DoD field: two clauses moved to spun-out rows.

WHY. The row as written needs ~20 distinct files, over the daemon's 10-file hard reject. The forcing measurement, all reproducible at HEAD on moe/work-2026-09-04:
(1) `moe-wrapper` (orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts) and `moe-daemon` (daemon-main.ts) are SEPARATE bin entries in apps/daemon/package.json — separate OS processes sharing only the SQLite store.
(2) `createRepositoryDeliveryRuntime` — the node lander, the ONLY writer of `outcome: "COMMITTED"` (node-lander.ts:255) — is constructed at agent-wrapper-main.ts:160 and nowhere else. So a landing hook runs in the WRAPPER.
(3) `createPreviewSupervisor` holds live previews in an in-memory Map (preview-supervisor.ts:56). A preview started in the wrapper is invisible to the daemon: `decide()` finds nothing to stop, and daemon shutdown cannot sweep it.
(4) `preview.decide` is served by the DAEMON command plane, so the supervisor must live in the daemon.
(5) `git grep -n "setInterval" -- apps/daemon/src` → ZERO production hits. The daemon has no tick loop, and an affordance READ must not spawn a product server.
Therefore the START must be a daemon COMMAND, and since `runPreview` spawns a dev server and drives Playwright it must be an ASYNC entry. A new runtime kind is unavoidable — and epic rail 1 makes the shared-contract slice its own row.

THE SPLIT (children filed in PLANNING per global rail 20, dependsOn set):
- task-0e87ab347a6a42bda88d1ec539c01731 — preview.start on the shared runtime roster + every digest mirror + regenerated client. dependsOn [] (LEAF).
- task-dbc79d2556ab44bbbf87e2194d9e9e53 — preview.start as an async daemon command writing the receipt. dependsOn [task-0e87ab34, THIS ROW].
- task-33ceae56 (Gate 2 browser proof) repointed to also dependsOn task-dbc79d25. dependsOnUnmet 2.

CLAUSE → ROW MAP. THIS ROW keeps DoD 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8 and the SECOND clause of 7.
- DoD 3 (a preview can be STARTED by a production path) → task-dbc79d25.
- DoD 7 first clause (new kind rotates contract + mirrors + client + control-room leg) → task-0e87ab34 (contract half) and task-dbc79d25 (daemon half). THIS ROW ADDS NO NEW COMMAND KIND — DoD 7's own escape hatch applies and the worker states that plainly.
DoD 4 STAYS HERE and is fully reachable without the start command: the offer keys on a receipt read through `readPreviewReceipt`, and a STARTED/REFUSED receipt is established in the arm by `recordPreviewReceipt` — the PRODUCTION writer, not a mock. Only the receipt's operator TRIGGER is deferred.

BUILD ORDER (global rail 17: plan the leaf first). THIS ROW IS THE LEAF and lands FIRST — its own dependsOn (task-f5a74c23, task-40e52fa8) are both DONE. It deletes the fail-closed stub at daemon-command-registry.ts:438 and composes the supervisor into the daemon; the children then hang the start command off the port it composes. Note the direction: children depend on the parent here, which is why this row's dependsOn is NOT widened (global rail 24's parent→child form does not fit a leaf-first split; the ordering is still declared as fields, on the children).

DoD ERRATUM, measured: item 7 says "all four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors". At HEAD there are SIX. `git grep -n 9057aa947ce5cd23c1e2e667ddbf9315a7e329869a4fa0d473e037cd1d30077d` (tracked, minus .moe/) → generated-client.ts:935, generated-coverage.test.ts:36, data-adapter.test.ts:18, approve-plan.test.tsx:255, approve-plan-reject.test.tsx:110, plan-run-resolution.test.tsx:149. Epic rail 3 in the wild — the DoD froze a count a peer row moved. Carried into task-0e87ab34 as a re-measure instruction, not a value.

@governors: requesting the DoD field on THIS ROW be narrowed to items 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8 + item 7's second clause, with 3 and 7-first-clause recorded as carried by the two children named above. No architect tool edits the DoD field; this comment is the record until that lands.

Plan touches 9 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
START TRIGGER — four designs evaluated, three rejected on measurement. (a) Goal-lifecycle hook off the node lander: REJECTED, `createRepositoryDeliveryRuntime` is constructed only at agent-wrapper-main.ts:160, and `moe-wrapper`/`moe-daemon` are separate bin entries in apps/daemon/package.json, so the hook runs in a DIFFERENT PROCESS from the supervisor's in-memory Map (preview-supervisor.ts:56) and from the `preview.decide` command plane — decide would find nothing to stop and daemon shutdown could not sweep it. (b) Lazy start from the affordance READ: REJECTED, a polled GET must not spawn a product server, and `resolvePlanningOffers` is synchronous while `supervisor.start` is async — it would be an unhandled fire-and-forget with no backpressure. (c) A daemon interval sweeper: REJECTED, `git grep -n "setInterval" -- apps/daemon/src` returns ZERO production hits; the daemon is command/read-driven by design and inventing a loop here is a much larger change than this row. (d) CHOSEN: an async daemon command — but that is a NEW runtime kind, which epic rail 1 makes a separate row, so it is spun out as task-0e87ab34 (contract) + task-dbc79d25 (daemon half). THIS ROW IS THE LEAF and lands first.

EDGE PLACEMENT — daemon-command-registry.ts is 531 lines, already past the 400-line split threshold, so the decide edge gets its own module rather than a fatter branch. That matches how daemon-command-async-entries.ts justifies its own existence in its header comment.

SHUTDOWN SEAM — `StoreDependencyProvider.close()` is SYNC and has six call sites (mcp-main.ts:158, agent-wrapper-main.ts:366, and four fixtures). Widening it to async is out of scope and would blow the file budget. Use the daemon's ALREADY-ASYNC shutdown instead: daemon-entry.ts:333 `await started.close()`.

FILE BUDGET — this plan is at NINE distinct files against the cap of ten. preview-contracts.ts, preview-ledger.ts, preview-supervisor.ts, preview-goal-landing.ts and preview-test-fixtures.ts are READ in step 1 and imported thereafter but never MODIFIED, so they are deliberately absent from affectedFiles; they are listed in keyFiles instead. If a step turns out to need an edit to any of them, that is a tenth file — still inside budget — but a request to edit an ELEVENTH means stop and report rather than trimming coverage.

DoD 3 and DoD 7's first clause are carried by the two spun-out children (see comment-0fe1031487b84ee6a0b8c2d7fb004ef0 and the @governors post). This row adds NO new command kind — DoD 7's second clause applies and must be stated plainly in the completion record.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD ON moe/work-2026-09-04 (commands and results; global rail 6 — re-measure, do not trust the description).

THE GAP IS REAL, all four legs reproduce:
1. `grep -n "preview runner is not landed"` -> exactly 1 hit, daemon-command-registry.ts:440. The block at :434-441 decodes the payload then unconditionally throws `previewRefusal("PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED")`. Its own comment at :432 calls it "the FAIL-CLOSED stub the runner replaces".
2. `git grep -n "createPreviewRunner\|createPreviewSupervisor\|recordPreviewReceipt\|runPreview" -- apps packages ':!apps/daemon/src/preview/*'` -> ZERO.
3. `git grep -n "preview\.start" -- apps packages` -> ZERO.
4. `git grep -in preview -- 'apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-*.ts'` minus tests -> ZERO.
ONE THING THE DESCRIPTION GOT STALE: `git grep -n "preview/preview-"` outside the preview dir now returns SIX hits, not four — environment/environment-delivery.ts:25 and its test import `startPreviewProcess`. Still only preview-contracts + preview-process; the runner/supervisor/ledger remain unreachable.

CONTENTION WARNING IS STALE: the three rows the description names (task-a2409cba, task-c422b106, task-166d375f) are NOT on this epic's 32-row roster. Do not plan around them; still never freeze a roster count (epic rail 3).

THE SEAMS THIS ROW USES, all landed and read at HEAD (READ-ONLY — none of these files is modified by this row):
- `decodePreviewDecidePayload(payload)` (preview-contracts.ts:225) returns `{ok:true,payload:{decision,previewRef[,findings]}}` or a `previewRefusal("PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID")`. `previewRef` IS the receipt id.
- `previewRefusal(code)` (preview-contracts.ts:142) takes NO layer; `PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS` (:82) is the closed map and `PREVIEW_CODES` is its key set.
- `readPreviewReceipt(store, projectId, receiptId)` (preview-ledger.ts:81) -> `{ok:true,receipt}` | `{ok:false,code:"PREVIEW_RECEIPT_INVALID"|"PREVIEW_RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND"}`. It re-validates principal, kind and project against the record, so a decision written under another principal can never read back as a receipt.
- `recordPreviewReceipt(store, input)` (preview-ledger.ts:100) is the PRODUCTION writer, idempotent by `previewReceiptId(projectId, goalId, sha)` and answers `replayed:true` on a repeat. It records STARTED or REFUSED-with-code. Use it to establish receipt state in arms — it is production, not a mock.
- `createPreviewSupervisor(config)` (preview-supervisor.ts:55) exposes `active()`, `close()`, `decide(receiptId, decision)`, `start(request)`. `close()` deliberately does not throw on a straggler; liveness is asserted BY PID.
- `readGoalLandingStatus(store, projectId, goalId, folded?)` (preview-goal-landing.ts:73) -> `{allLanded, missing[], nodes[]}`; a goal with no execution-bearing node reports NOT landed rather than vacuously landed.
- `preview-test-fixtures.ts:124 awaitPidGone` wraps the PRODUCTION probe `probeProcessAlive` (orchestrator/process-runner-lifecycle.ts:48) with 200x50ms. Reuse it; do NOT write a third liveness helper.

OFFER LADDER PATTERN (copy it exactly): `PlanningOfferInput` (affordance-planning-offers.ts:36-64) takes FACTS, not store handles, and they are LAZY — `closeReadiness`, `currentRun`, `landedCommit`. The ladder stays pure; the composition root at affordance-read.ts:298-317 supplies them (`landedCommit: landings.hasLandedCommit`). Offers are minted by the local `offer(input, kind, target)` helper at :126. Add `previewReceipt: (goalId) => "STARTED"|"REFUSED"|null` the same way and resolve it in affordance-read.ts from `readPreviewReceipt`.

RUNTIME-TIER TRAP THAT COST task-f5a74c23 A ROUND: runtime-entrypoint.test.ts builds `runtimeTierModules` (:155) from the entry module plus every module carrying its OWN `<name>.test.ts` sibling, then asserts `{missing:[],unexpected:[],wrongContent:[]}` (:255). A new module with a `.js` bridge but a differently-named test file is classified TEST tier and its bridge comes back as `unexpected`. Name the test file to match the module EXACTLY. Expected disclosed `unexpected` at filing time is ONE entry, `repository\deployment\deployment-docker-probe.js`; anything containing `preview\` is this row's bug.

GATE SHAPE: the root `pnpm test` include has NO apps/**, so it covers nothing here. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` was 13 failed / 491 passed FILES, exit 1, ~750s at the last preview row (foreign red, zero under src/preview). `pnpm typecheck` was exit 1 on peer src/repository only. Attribute by merge-base-vs-HEAD (global rail 3) and disclose verbatim.
planningNotes.risks:
1. RUNTIME-TIER BRIDGE. A new module under src/preview shipping a `.js` bridge MUST have a name-matched `<module>.test.ts`. Mismatch = `unexpected` entry in runtime-entrypoint.test.ts, hidden inside a suite already red for a dozen foreign reasons. Read the ARRAY, not the pass/fail.
2. VACUOUS REFUSAL ARMS (global rail 1). The stub makes EVERY well-formed decide throw PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED today, so a test asserting merely "preview.decide refuses" is green before and after this row and proves nothing. Each of the four arms must make every OTHER gate passable so it pins WHICH layer answered, and each must be mutation-drilled against the production surface.
